proposal: This combo is not an untap loop but a bounce-and-recast loop: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds taps for X mana (X = greatest power among creatures you control, here 7+), then Temur Sabertooth's {1}{G} ability returns Selvala to hand (no untap ability is involved), Selvala is recast for its commander cost {1}{G}{G}, and Lightning Greaves (equip {0}) re-attaches to grant haste so the summoning-sick Selvala can tap again immediately. A fitting archetype would be a 'TapForManaBounceRecastLoop' parameterized by engine, bouncer, bounce_cost ({1}{G}), recast_cost ({1}{G}{G} plus commander tax growth), haste_enabler (Lightning Greaves) with attach_cost ({0}), activation_cost ({G}), yield_expr GREATEST_POWER_AMONG_OWN_CREATURES, and a profit invariant of yield minus per-cycle costs (~5 mana) > 0; the loop also generates infinite ETB/LTB and storm triggers per cycle, which the untap archetype cannot model.

This combo is a bounce-and-recast mana loop, not an untap loop: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds taps for X = greatest power among your creatures (needs a power-6+ creature), Temur Sabertooth's '{1}{G}: return another creature you control to hand' bounces Selvala instead of untapping her, and she is recast for {1}{G}{G} and can re-tap immediately only because Concordant Crossroads grants haste. A new archetype (e.g. BounceRecastManaLoop) would need params: engine (Selvala, activation_cost {G}, pool_color G, yield GREATEST_POWER_AMONG_OWN_CREATURES), bouncer (Temur Sabertooth, bounce_cost {1}{G}, nontargeted, bounces to owner's hand), engine_recast_cost {1}{G}{G} paid each cycle (plus commander-tax awareness since Selvala is the commander), a required haste_enabler on the battlefield (Concordant Crossroads), and profit_invariant yield - 5 > 0; the loop additionally produces infinite ETB/LTB triggers, storm count, and (via Selvala's own trigger) card draw as side products, which TapForManaUntapLoop cannot model since it assumes the engine stays on the battlefield and merely untaps.

This combo is a bounce-and-recast loop, not a tap-untap loop: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds ({G}, {T}) adds X mana equal to the greatest power among creatures you control, Temur Sabertooth ({1}{G}) returns Selvala to hand instead of untapping her, Selvala is recast for her mana cost {1}{G}{G}, and Surrak and Goreclaw grants the re-entering Selvala haste (plus a +1/+1 counter) so she can tap again immediately. A fitting new archetype would be 'TapForManaBounceRecastLoop' with params: engine (the mana creature), bouncer, bounce_cost, engine_recast_cost, haste_granter (static permanent removing summoning sickness on re-entry), activation_cost, per_cycle_counter_pump (power gained per re-entry from ETB counters, non-cumulative since counters are lost on bounce), pool_color, and a profit invariant of yield minus (activation + bounce + recast) > 0; each cycle also generates one ETB/LTB/cast trigger for storm and blink payoffs.

This combo is a three-piece chained untap loop that does not fit TapForManaUntapLoop's two-piece (engine + untapper) shape: Gaea's Cradle is the mana engine ({T}: Add {G} for each creature you control, at least {G}{G}{G}{G}{G} given five creatures), Voyaging Satyr is the primary untapper ({T}: Untap target land, targeting the Cradle), but the Satyr cannot re-ready itself — it requires a second untapper, Staff of Domination ({3}, {T}: Untap target creature, targeting the Satyr; then {1}: Untap Staff of Domination to reset itself). Binding Satyr as 'untapper' with untapper_reset_cost {4} would misrepresent the reset as a self-ability and omit Staff of Domination from the binding entirely, so simulation would not exercise the actual pieces. A new archetype such as ChainedTapForManaUntapLoop is needed, with params: engine (Gaea's Cradle, activation_cost {0}, dynamic yield GG*CREATURES_YOU_CONTROL, pool_color G), untapper_1 (Voyaging Satyr, untap_cost {0}, targets engine), untapper_2 (Staff of Domination, untap_cost {3}, targets untapper_1, self_reset_cost {1}), net profit per cycle = creatures_you_control - 4 > 0 (hence the five-creature prerequisite), with Staff's {5} draw ability as the DRAW_LOOP stage payoff.

This combo is not an untap loop — Sanctum Weaver never untaps; instead Temur Sabertooth's {1}{G} activation bounces the Weaver to hand, it is recast for {1}{G}, and Concordant Crossroads grants haste so it can tap again the same turn. A new archetype, e.g. BounceRecastManaLoop, is needed with params: engine (Sanctum Weaver, a creature tapped for X mana where X scales with enchantments controlled), bouncer (Temur Sabertooth), bounce_cost ({1}{G}), recast_cost (the engine's mana cost {1}{G}), haste_enabler (Concordant Crossroads, required because the engine re-enters each cycle), yield_expr (COUNT_OWN_ENCHANTMENTS, noting the Weaver itself is an enchantment creature so the count dips by one while it is off the battlefield), pool_color (any one color, engine's choice), and a profit_invariant of yield - 4 > 0 per cycle (X mana in vs {1}{G} bounce + {1}{G} recast), matching the 'at least four enchantments' prerequisite; the loop additionally produces infinite ETB/LTB triggers and storm count as side effects.
